key_insight: Utonia demonstrates that a single self-supervised point-transformer encoder can be trained on a large, diverse mix of point-cloud domains (remote sensing, LiDAR, RGB‑D, CAD, and video-lifted clouds) to learn consistent, transferable 3D representations despite differing sensing geometries and densities.
problem_solved: Addresses fragmentation in 3D modeling where separate encoders are needed per sensing domain by bridging domain gaps and enabling one unified encoder that generalizes across varied point‑cloud sources.
method: Pretrain a single transformer-based point encoder self-supervised on a heterogeneous collection of point-cloud datasets covering multiple domains and sensors.
Use domain-aware sampling, positional encoding, and augmentation strategies to handle differing densities and sensing geometries so all domains can be learned jointly.
Optimize alignment-promoting self-supervised objectives (e.g., contrastive or reconstruction-style losses) to produce robust, cross-domain representations usable for many downstream tasks.
impact: Provides a path toward unified 3D pretraining that reduces the need for domain-specific models, improving transferability, sample efficiency, and deployment simplicity for downstream 3D tasks across robotics, remote sensing, AR/VR, and autonomous driving.
visual_elements: Multi-domain collage: icons or sample point-clouds from remote sensing, outdoor LiDAR, indoor RGB‑D, CAD, and video-lifted clouds to show training diversity.
Architecture diagram: single transformer encoder block with inputs from different domains and domain-aware encoding/highlighting of shared weights.
Embedding alignment plot: t-SNE/UMAP showing clusters from different domains overlapping after Utonia pretraining.
Performance chart: bar or radar chart comparing downstream task performance (or robustness) of Utonia vs. domain-specific baselines.
paper_title: Utonia: Toward One Encoder for All Point Clouds
paper_authors: Yujia Zhang, Xiaoyang Wu, Yunhan Yang, Xianzhe Fan, Han Li
